title: Pharmacological targets and validation of remdesivir for the treatment of COVID-19-associated pulmonary fibrosis: A network-based pharmacology and bioinformatics study.
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过网络药理学和生物信息学分析瑞德西韦治疗COVID-19相关肺纤维化的靶点与机制，虽涉及转录因子和分子对接，但核心是药物-疾病网络而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，方法以数据库和富集分析为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟的深度建模。
abstract: The objective of this study was to employ bioinformatics and network pharmacology methodologies to investigate the targets and molecular mechanisms of remdesivir in the treatment of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-associated pulmonary fibrosis (PF). Several open-source databases were utilized to confirm the shared targets of remdesivir, COVID-19, and PF. Following this, a comprehensive analysis incorporating function enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI), transcription factor (TF), and molecular docking was conducted to investigate the potential mechanisms underlying the effectiveness of remdesivir in the treatment of COVID-19-associated PF. The initial validation of these findings was performed using publicly available histological and single-cell sequencing databases. The functional enrichment analysis revealed a strong association between remdesivir and viral defense, inflammatory response, and immune response. The key pathways identified in the study were transforming growth factor (TGF-beta), PI3K-Akt, mTOR, MAPK, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance, HIF-1, and Toll-like receptor signaling pathways. Additionally, the PPI analysis demonstrated the network relationships of 13 important targets, while the TF analysis provided valuable insights into the regulatory networks of these targets. Among the identified TFs, RELA was found to be the most significant. To validate our findings, we utilized publicly available histological and single-cell sequencing databases, successfully confirming the involvement of 8 key targets, including AKT1, EGFR, RHOA, MAPK1, PIK3R1, MAPK8, MAPK14, and MTOR. Furthermore, molecular docking studies were conducted to assess the interaction between remdesivir and the identified key targets, thus confirming its effective targeting effects. Remdesivir has the potential to exert antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory effects in the context of COVID-19-associated PF.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在运用生物信息学和网络药理学方法，探讨瑞德西韦治疗2019冠状病毒病（COVID-19）相关肺纤维化（PF）的靶点及分子机制。利用多个开源数据库确认瑞德西韦、COVID-19和PF的共同靶点。随后，结合功能富集、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）、转录因子（TF）和分子对接进行综合分析，以探究瑞德西韦治疗COVID-19相关PF潜在机制。初步验证采用公开可用的组织学和单细胞测序数据库进行。功能富集分析显示，瑞德西韦与病毒防御、炎症反应和免疫反应密切相关。研究中确定的关键通路包括转化生长因子（TGF-beta）、PI3K-Akt、mTOR、MAPK、表皮生长因子受体（EGFR）酪氨酸激酶抑制剂耐药性、HIF-1和Toll样受体信号通路。此外，PPI分析展示了13个重要靶点的网络关系，而TF分析为这些靶点的调控网络提供了宝贵见解。在识别的TF中，RELA被认为是最重要的。为验证我们的发现，利用公开的组织学和单细胞测序数据库，成功确认了8个关键靶点的参与，包括AKT1、EGFR、RHOA、MAPK1、PIK3R1、MAPK8、MAPK14和MTOR。此外，进行了分子对接研究以评估瑞德西韦与已识别关键靶点之间的相互作用，从而确认其有效的靶向作用。瑞德西韦在COVID-19相关PF背景下具有潜在的抗病毒、抗炎和免疫调节作用。
